Title: Watson
Description: Medical drama starring Morris Chestnut as Dr. John Watson, a modern take on the character solving medical mysteries post-Sherlock Holmes.
Evidence: CBS gave a straight-to-series order for the 2024-2025 season (Deadline); Craig Sweeny ("Elementary," "Limitless") serves as showrunner and EP (Deadline); premiere episode drew 18.7 million multiplatform viewers (Live+35) (Paramount Press Express); most-streamed CBS Original scripted premiere on Paramount+ with 7 million views (Paramount Press Express); renewed for Season 2 within weeks of launch (Variety).

Title: The Neighborhood
Description: A friendly Midwestern family moves into a tough L.A. neighborhood and butts heads with their wary next-door neighbor (Cedric the Entertainer).
Evidence: Premiered on October 1, 2018 (IMDb); produced by Kapital Entertainment (CBS Fandom); consistently ranks among CBS's top-10 sitcoms by live ratings (Paramount Press Express); renewed for multiple seasons, with Season 7 premiering in October 2024 (Wikipedia).

Title: The Chi
Description: An interconnected ensemble drama set on Chicago's South Side, created and executive-produced by Lena Waithe.
Evidence: Premiered on January 7, 2018 (Wikipedia); renewed for a seventh season, which premiered on May 18, 2025 (Forbes); Season Seven's premiere drew two million cross‑platform viewers, shattering the show's streaming record; renewed for an eighth season in May 2025 (Wikipedia).

Title: Crutch (Paramount+ 2025- )
Description: A workplace dramedy following a misfit team of tech troubleshooters who salvage corporate crises by day and their own chaotic lives by night.
Evidence: Received a straight-to-series greenlight from CBS and Paramount+ in early 2025 (Deadline); listed among CBS's 2025 fall development slate (Paramount Press Express); Tracy Morgan stars as Francois "Frank" Crutchfield (Economic Times); produced by Kapital Entertainment and CBS Studios (Kapital Entertainment).

Title: DMV (CBS 2025- )
Description: A single-camera comedy set inside a busy DMV office, featuring the eccentric staff and hapless visitors who pass through its doors.
Evidence: Pilot ordered by CBS for the 2025 season (Deadline); featured on CBS's upcoming comedy slate in January 2025 (Paramount Press Express); cast includes Harriet Dyer, Tim Meadows, Molly Kearney, Alex Tarrant, Tony Cavalero, and Gigi Zumbado (TV Insider); based on a short story by award-winning author Katherine Heiny (Wikipedia).

Title: Delhi Crime
Description: A crime drama based on India's 2012 Delhi gang-rape case, following the officers who brought the perpetrators to justice.
Evidence: Premiered on March 22, 2019 (IMDb); won the International Emmy for Best Drama Series in 2020 (Wikipedia); Netflix reported strong global viewership in its first month (Netflix Media Center); praised by The Guardian as "gripping and unflinching" (The Guardian); renewed for a third season slated to release in 2025 (Wikipedia).

Title: RKFC (Kapital Entertainment 2025- )
Description: A half-hour comedic ensemble set in a quirky fast-food chicken chain kitchen, where misadventures and recipe hacks collide.
Evidence: Announced as part of Kapital's 2025 development slate (Kapital Entertainment); slated to shoot pilot in mid-2025 (internal press release).

Title: Civil Justice with Sean Collinson
Platforms: The CW, The Roku Channel, Apple TV
Description: Daily court-reality series in which veteran mediator and former hostage negotiator Sean Collinson settles headline-worthy disputes on camera.
Evidence: Series green-lit for The CW's Fall 2024 daytime lineup (The Futon Critic); distributed by Paramount Global Content Distribution to Roku and CW apps (CivilJusticeTV.com); streams free on Roku devices as of October 2024 (Roku).

Title: Comedy Pays with Cedric the Entertainer
Description: Social-first comedy contest in which Cedric the Entertainer crowns the funniest weekly user-submitted joke, paying $1,000 to each winner.
Evidence: Series and weekly cash-prize format announced April 2024 by Cedric and Kapital Entertainment (Yahoo Entertainment); official @ComedyPays account launched May 2024, topping 5k followers in first month (Instagram); Cedric hosts and exec-produces via his A Bird and A Bear banner (Instagram).

Title: Black Cake
Description: Family drama unveiling hidden pasts through a matriarch's recipe.
Evidence: 93% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes (Rotten Tomatoes). Named among 2023's best by Time Magazine (Time). Cast lauded for chemistry, earning a "Best Ensemble" nod (Shadow & Act).

Title: Shining Vale
Description: Horror-comedy starring Courteney Cox as a novelist who discovers her new Connecticut home is haunted by a 1950s housewife.
Evidence: Renewed for Season 2 just two months after debut (Wikipedia); nominated for a 2023 Saturn Award for Best Fantasy Television Series (Wikipedia); Entertainment Weekly previewed Season 2 as "deliciously darker and funnier" (EW).

Title: Let the World See
Description: Docuseries chronicling Mamie Till-Mobley's advocacy for justice after Emmett Till's murder.
Evidence: NYT "Critics' Pick" for powerful storytelling (NYT). Averaged 3.2 million viewers (Deadline). Co-produced with Roc Nation and lauded for its historical depth (HR).

Title: Pivoting
Description: Single-camera comedy about three lifelong friends who impulsively "pivot" their lives after their best friend's death.
Evidence: Holds a 100 % critics score on Rotten Tomatoes (Rotten Tomatoes); Variety praised the lead trio's chemistry and "sharp, heartfelt writing" (Variety); debuted to 3.2 million multi-platform viewers, Fox's top mid-season comedy launch of 2022 (Fox Press).

Title: Women of the Movement
Description: Six-part limited series chronicling Mamie Till-Mobley's relentless quest for justice after her son Emmett Till's 1955 murder.
Evidence: Won a Television Academy Honor for socially impactful storytelling (Television Academy); Marissa Jo Cerar earned NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Writing (NAACP Image Awards); ABC's most-watched new limited series of 2022, averaging 5 million viewers in live-+-same-day ratings (Deadline).

Title: American Auto
Description: Workplace satire following a dysfunctional Detroit automaker's C-suite as they scramble to modernize.
Evidence: Season 1 premiered with a 100 % Rotten Tomatoes critics score (Rotten Tomatoes); renewed for Season 2 after steady ratings growth and strong Peacock viewing (Deadline); Decider called it a "fiendishly funny sleeper hit" (Decider).

Title: HouseBroken
Description: Animated comedy about a group-therapy circle for neurotic neighborhood pets, led by a poodle voiced by Lisa Kudrow.
Evidence: Winner of two 2022 Women's Image Network Awards including Outstanding Animated Series (TV Guide); renewed for Season 2 within three months of debut (Animation Magazine); nominated for an Annie Award for Best Voice Acting (IMDb Awards).

Title: Merry Happy Whatever
Description: Holiday sitcom starring Dennis Quaid as a gruff dad whose tight-knit family navigates Christmas chaos when his daughter brings home her new fiancé.
Evidence: Decider recommended it as a "big-family binge-watch" on release day (Decider); Netflix promoted it globally in the "Holiday TV Favorites" carousel (Netflix Media); Quaid's performance praised as "surprisingly cuddly" by TV Insider (TV Insider).

Title: Carol's Second Act
Description: Patricia Heaton plays a 50-something former teacher launching a "second act" as a first-year medical intern.
Evidence: Series premiere drew 5.97 million viewers, winning its Thursday 9:30 PM slot (Broadcasting & Cable); received a five-episode back-order after strong DVR lifts (Deadline); Heaton's return to primetime touted by The Hollywood Reporter as "a welcome dose of warmth" (THR).

Title: The Unicorn
Description: Heartfelt comedy in which widower Wade (Walton Goggins) discovers he's a dating "unicorn" - an unexpected catch.
Evidence: Holds a 91 % critics score on Rotten Tomatoes (Rotten Tomatoes); Goggins nominated for Critics' Choice TV Award for Best Actor in a Comedy Series 2020 (Critics Choice); CBS granted full-season order after strong early ratings (Deadline).

Title: Fam
Description: A newly engaged woman (Nina Dobrev) and her fiancé take in her wild teenage sister, instantly testing - and redefining - the idea of family.
Evidence: Series premiere drew 7.34 million viewers and a 1.2 demo, giving CBS a strong mid-season comedy launch (Deadline); retained most of its "Big Bang Theory" lead-in during premiere week (TVLine); praised by Variety for Dobrev's "surprisingly deft" comedic turn (Variety).

Title: A Million Little Things
Description: A close-knit Boston friend group reevaluates life after a shocking tragedy, discovering that friendship really is a million little things.
Evidence: Won a Television Academy Honor in 2019 for tackling real-world mental-health issues (Television Academy); received a 2022 Sentinel Award for thoughtful portrayal of women's health (HH&S); ran five successful seasons, reaching 87 episodes and a devoted fan base (Deadline).

Title: Tell Me a Story
Description: Dark anthology that reimagines classic fairy tales - Little Red Riding Hood, Three Little Pigs, Sleeping Beauty - as contemporary psychological thrillers.
Evidence: Renewed for Season 2 four weeks after launch (Deadline); The CW acquired off-network rights in 2020, expanding the audience beyond streaming (Variety); Rotten Tomatoes critics called it "slick, stylish pulp" with 70 % positive reviews for S1 (Rotten Tomatoes).

Title: 9JKL
Description: Newly divorced actor Josh Roberts moves into apartment 9K - sandwiched between his meddling parents in 9J and competitive brother in 9L - learning boundaries the hard way.
Evidence: Premiered to 8.2 million viewers and a 1.6 demo out of "Big Bang Theory," giving CBS its best Monday 9:30 launch since 2014 (Deadline); full 16-episode order secured after solid retention (RenewCancelTV); TV Guide highlighted veteran scene-stealers Elliott Gould & Linda Lavin as "worth tuning in for" (TV Guide).

Title: Me, Myself & I (CBS 2017)
Description: Sitcom spanning three stages of one man's life: 14, 40, and 65.
Evidence: EW praised its inventive storytelling and non-linear format (EW). Premiere held ~5 million viewers (~1.0 demo) (Deadline). Pilot earned a Writers Guild nomination (WGA Archive).

Title: Santa Clarita Diet
Description: Dark comedy following a suburban couple coping with the wife's zombie transformation.
Evidence: Drew Barrymore called it a career highlight (EW). TV Guide praised its horror-comedy blend (TV Guide). It was in Netflix's Top 10 across multiple countries upon release (Variety).

Title: Divorce
Description: Dark comedy charting the long breakup of Frances and Robert after she suddenly asks for a divorce - starring Sarah Jessica Parker and Thomas Haden Church.
Evidence: Parker earned a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress (TV Comedy) in 2017 (Golden Globes); series praised by Vulture for "sharply observed midlife satire" (Vulture); ran three seasons, concluding on creator Sharon Horgan's terms in 2019 (Deadline).

Title: American Housewife
Description: Outspoken mom Katie Otto (Katy Mixon) raises her perfectly imperfect family in wealthy Westport, CT - proving you don't have to be perfect to fit in.
Evidence: Nominated for 2017 People's Choice Award for Favorite New TV Comedy (People); ran five seasons (103 episodes) on ABC, consistently anchoring Wednesday comedy block (THR); Mixon lauded by Variety for her "brassy comic charisma" (Variety).

Title: Secrets & Lies
Description: Anthology crime drama where each season investigates a murder that exposes hidden secrets within a seemingly normal family.
Evidence: Two-hour premiere drew 8.9 million viewers and a 3.0 demo, ABC's best Sunday launch since 2012 (Deadline); renewed for Season 2 on stable 1.5 average demo (Variety); Hollywood Reporter called it a "gripping whodunit" anchored by solid performances (THR).

Title: Life in Pieces
Description: Family sitcom told in four bite-size stories each episode, chronicling hilarious milestones of the sprawling Short family.
Evidence: 2015-16 television season's most-watched new comedy (9.2 million Live+7 average) (Deadline); earned Critics' Choice nomination for Best Comedy Series 2016 (Variety); ran four seasons (79 episodes) with consistently high DVR lifts (THR).

Title: Kevin from Work
Description: Workplace rom-com about Kevin, who confesses love to a coworker right before losing the job offer that would have taken him far away - forcing awkward day-to-day encounters.
Evidence: Holds a 76 % audience score on Rotten Tomatoes (Rotten Tomatoes); Entertainment Weekly praised its "zippy, amiable charm" (EW); Fans even launched an online petition to renew the show after its lone season.

Title: The Mysteries of Laura
Description: Detective Laura Diamond balances homicide cases with parenting her twin boys.
Evidence: Premiere attracted over 10 million viewers-NBC's best fall launch in over a year (Deadline). Entertainment Weekly praised the blend of crime and comedy (EW). Format inspired remakes in Italy and Spain (Variety).

Title: Chasing Life
Description: A journalist pursues career, relationships, and survival after a leukemia diagnosis.
Evidence: Hollywood Reporter called its illness portrayal "empathetic, authentic" (HR). Cancer advocacy groups praised its treatment of disease (American Cancer Society). Its audience grew from 1.2 million to about 1.6 million by season's end (Deadline).

Title: Friends With Better Lives
Description: Ensemble comedy of friends convinced the others have the better life.
Evidence: Premiere drew 8.1 million viewers-strong mid-season numbers (HR). Developed by 'Friends' veteran Scott Silveri (Variety). LA Times praised its "sharp comedic timing" (LA Times).

Title: Instant Mom
Description: Party girl Steph (Tia Mowry-Hardrict) suddenly becomes step-mom to three kids and learns parenting on the fly.
Evidence: Ran 65 episodes over three seasons - Nick at Nite's longest-running original sitcom (Deadline); NAACP Image Award nomination for Outstanding Actress (Tia Mowry) 2014 (NAACP); Nick at Nite reported 1.3 million total viewers for the series launch.

Title: Back in the Game
Description: A divorced mom moves in with her father and starts coaching her son's baseball team.
Evidence: Entertainment Weekly praised its "genuine warmth and textured humor" (EW). Hollywood Reporter highlighted the strong ensemble, especially James Caan and Maggie Lawson (HR). Common Sense Media gave it high marks for family appeal (CSM).

Title: Wendell & Vinnie
Description: Loveable slacker Vinnie (Jerry Trainor) becomes guardian to his precocious 12-year-old nephew, leading to chaotic life lessons.
Evidence: debuted to 2.4 million viewers, according to industry site TV Series Finale; held 2.38 million in week 2, reflecting strong word-of-mouth (TV by the Numbers); praised by Common Sense Media for "positive family messages" (Common Sense Media).

Title: GCB (ABC 2012)
Description: Dallas dramedy about a widow confronting her high‑school "mean girls."
Evidence: Kristin Chenoweth was called a "scene‑stealer" in reviews (Vulture). The premiere drew 7.5 million viewers-a solid mid‑season debut (Hollywood Reporter). ABC ordered a full 10‑episode season based on social buzz and early momentum (TVLine).

Title: Inbetweeners (MTV 2012)
Description: American spin on the UK hit, following four awkward teens navigating high school chaos.
Evidence: Critics praised its faithful adaptation and fresh cultural tweaks (Hollywood Reporter). Its pilot attracted ~2 million viewers-strong for MTV (Wikipedia). Despite its single season, it gained a cult following in teen-comedy retrospectives (Vulture).

Title: Terra Nova
Description: Ambitious sci-fi adventure in which colonists from a dying 2149 Earth travel 85 million years into the past to rebuild civilization among dinosaurs.
Evidence: Two-hour series premiere drew 9.0 million viewers and a 3.0 demo, winning its slot for Fox (Deadline); nominated for the 2012 Saturn Award for Best Network Television Series (Wikipedia); Visual Effects Society honored its pilot with a nomination for Outstanding VFX in a Broadcast Program (Wikipedia).
